title: NY State Assembly · District 72
area: Northern Manhattan, including Washington Heights, Inwood and parts of Hamilton Heights.

context.text: Incumbent Manny De Los Santos (D, WFP) is unopposed on the November ballot. He defeated Francesca Castellanos in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 75.4% to 23.9%. The Republican and Working Families Party primaries scheduled for that date were canceled.

candidates.name: Manny De Los Santos
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 75.4% of the vote; unopposed in the general election.
candidates.currentRole: NY State Assembly Member, District 72 (since February 2022)

summary.text: Manny De Los Santos is the Democratic and Working Families Party nominee for re-election in NY State Assembly District 72, running unopposed. Born in the Dominican Republic and raised in Northern Manhattan, he worked for 13 years as a social worker and community school director in New York City public schools before winning a February 2022 special election to the Assembly seat covering Washington Heights, Inwood and Marble Hill. He serves on the Banks, Education, Mental Health, Small Business, Social Services and Transportation committees.

background.text: Born in the Dominican Republic; according to his Assembly biography he was raised in Northern Manhattan and attended public schools. Lives in Washington Heights.
Earned a bachelor's degree in psychology and a master's degree in social work from the University at Albany (SUNY).
Worked for 13 years as a social worker and community school director in New York City public schools.

Served on the Neighborhood Advisory Board (NAB) and Manhattan Community Board 12 before his election; his Assembly biography says he coordinated voter registration and census drives and organized tenant, housing and immigration forums.
Ran in the September 9, 2014 Democratic primary for Assembly District 72, which Guillermo Linares won.

Won the February 15, 2022 special general election for Assembly District 72 as the Democratic candidate, defeating Nayma Silver-Matos (Uptown Rises) and Edwin De La Cruz (Republican); his predecessor was Carmen N. De La Rosa. He was re-elected in 2022 and 2024.

Serves on the Assembly's Banks, Education, Mental Health, Small Business, Social Services and Transportation committees, and is a member of the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislative Caucus and the Task Force on New Americans.

According to his Assembly biography, he has worked on school funding and on legislation to reduce class sizes statewide that passed; the Assembly's news page reports that Governor Hochul signed his lithium-ion battery safety bill in July 2024.

priorities.text: More funding for public schools; sponsored legislation to reduce class sizes statewide, which passed.
Promoting public safety in the district.
Creating more affordable housing options for working New Yorkers.
Ending reliance on fossil fuels to protect the environment and public health.

positions.summary: Says he is committed to ending New York's reliance on fossil fuels to protect the environment and public health.
positions.quote: ending our reliance on fossil fuels to protect our natural environment and our health

positions.summary: In a March 2026 club questionnaire, said he supports the unrestricted right to reproductive care and abortion.
positions.quote: I strongly support protecting access to reproductive healthcare and abortion rights.

positions.summary: In a March 2026 club questionnaire, committed to supporting legislation that raises taxes on the richest New Yorkers and large corporations.
positions.quote: I believe we must invest in housing, healthcare, education, transportation, and public services while ensuring the wealthiest individuals and corporations pay their fair share.

positions.summary: In a March 2026 club questionnaire, said he supports the goals of the New York for All Act, which limits state and local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: Yes, I support the goals of the New York for All Act and efforts to protect immigrant communities from harmful federal enforcement practices.

record.text: Sits on the Banks, Education, Mental Health, Small Business, Social Services and Transportation committees in the 2025-2026 session.
Sponsored legislation to reduce class sizes in New York public schools, which was signed into law.

candidates.researchNotes: De Los Santos has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey for 2026 and no separate campaign website (distinct from his official Assembly page) could be located, so most documented positions on the guide's fixed issue list beyond climate could not be confirmed directly from his own statements.
